liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- The first jam is described as smoking hot once the band settles into it [3]
- An early, embryonic version is tried after the surf jam, but nearly all of track 2 is silence [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **more bits of Lazy lightning and Slipknot, banter, ect**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [8]
- **some Blues For Allah bits**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [8]
- **jamming with Slipknot-type theme**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [8]

## The recordings

- **gd75-03-26.sbd.backus.14289.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 3 songs; 49 min; rated 2.33/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound quality resembles a telephone answering machine, and the session never really gets going; Sound is clear, studio-quality, and the reviewer says good equipment makes the jam better [2][5]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: some bits of Lazy Lightning and some tuning and [1]
- Track one opens with about ten minutes of mostly inaudible talk before the band starts its first jam [3]
- Much of the session is idle studio time, with Garcia noodling while everyone waits around [4]
- About ten minutes into track 1, a jam keeps nearly drifting into Goin' Down the Road, with Keith and Phil steering it funky [5]
- In track one, after a snappy Garcia guitar run, the band mentions The Yardbirds [7]
- Donna is absent; Billy is still on his own at the session [7]
- Music starts seven minutes into track 1 with a surf-style rock jam unlike anything else the Dead played [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd75-03-26.sbd.backus.14289.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard rehearsal tape, transferred via PCM and Prodif96Pro to WAV then SHN; part of a 6-disc set seeded to abgd; Terrapinstation re-shn'ed tracks 1 and 2 so they are seekable like the rest of the set [1]
